# instruction.md

## Poster Brief: JS Framework Benchmark — 5 Years of Browser Performance Testing

### Overview & Purpose

This poster tells the story of the JS Framework Benchmark — a long-running, community-critical project that has tracked JavaScript framework performance across 60+ official runs from Chrome 55 to Chrome 146. The audience is technically literate developers and engineering leads browsing a data-report-style document. The key message: this benchmark is massive in scope, has evolved significantly in methodology, and **cross-version comparisons are dangerous** without understanding those changes.

### Key Priorities

- **The timeline is the centerpiece.** The Chrome 55 → 146 journey spanning ~8 years should dominate the poster visually — think of a horizontal or vertical timeline strip that anchors the layout and immediately communicates scale and longevity.
- **Make the "60+" runs stat and the Chrome version range visually dominant.** These hero numbers should be the first things a viewer's eye lands on.
- **The methodology change at Chrome 118** (switch to weighted geometric mean) deserves a clear visual callout — it's the single most important reason cross-version comparisons break down. Treat it as a "caution" moment on the timeline.

### Visual & Style Guidance

Lean into a **dark-mode, developer-tool aesthetic** — think deep navy or charcoal backgrounds with vibrant accent colors (electric blue, teal, amber for warnings). Typography should be clean and monospaced for data labels, paired with a modern sans-serif for headings. The overall mood is precise, credible, and contemporary — like a well-designed engineering dashboard, not a marketing flyer. Use subtle grid lines or dot patterns to reinforce the data-forward tone.

---

## Data Sources

1. Read `/app/benchmark/source_brief.md` for all content materials (text, data, key messages).
2. Read `/app/benchmark/task_input.json` for poster requirements, sections, metrics, and style definitions.

## Output Requirements

1. Output the final poster to `/app/output/final_poster.png`.
2. The poster must be a single self-contained image file.

## Automated Execution Rules

There is no human operator online for this session. Follow these rules:

1. **Skip all confirmation/approval/user-input steps** — do not pause, ask questions, or wait for a reply. When encountering BLOCKING or wait-for-user instructions, make a professional judgment and continue.
2. **Design decisions** — if `task_input.json` specifies `poster.tone`, `poster.audience`, etc., use them to choose templates, palettes, and styles. Otherwise, make professional judgments.
3. **Priority** — these rules override any interactive-wait instructions in SKILL.md. The skill's workflow, quality standards, and technical specs remain fully effective — only skip interactive waits.

14	|---|---|---|---|
15	| Weighted Geometric Mean | 118 | 2023 | Overall score switched from arithmetic to weighted geometric mean |
16	| CPU Throttling Adjustment | 118 | 2023 | Throttling factors recalibrated for more realistic load simulation |
17	| Measurement Fine-Tuning | 118+ | 2023–present | Ongoing refinements to timing and driver instrumentation |
18	| Keyed-Only Alternation | 139+ | 2025–2026 | Odd Chrome versions often benchmark keyed frameworks only |
19	
20	Because of these evolving parameters, the project explicitly warns: *"Comparisons across Chrome versions aren't always safe since the benchmark and its driver are constantly developing."*
21

23

25	
26	| Year | Chrome Versions | Number of Runs | Notes |
27	|---|---|---|---|
28	| 2017–2019 | 55, 58, 62, 69 | 4 | Early era; hosted on stefankrause.net |
29	| 2020 | 83 – 87 | 5 | Migrated to GitHub Pages |
30	| 2021 | 88 – 96 | 9 | Steady monthly cadence established |
31	| 2022 | 97 – 108 | 13 | Includes 2 Windows runs (Chrome 104) |
32	| 2023 | 109 – 120 | 12 | Major methodology overhaul at Chrome 118 |
33	| 2024 | 121 – 131 | 12 | Includes 1 Windows run (Chrome 121) |
34	| 2025 | 132 – 143 | 12 | Most active year; alternating keyed-only runs |
35	| 2026 | 144 – 146 | 3 (so far) | Latest: Chrome 146 on macOS |
36	
37	## Platform Coverage
38	
39	The vast majority of runs — **over 95%** — were executed on **macOS (OSX)**. Only two Windows-specific runs exist:
40	
41	- **Chrome 104 – Windows** (2022)
42	- **Chrome 121 – Windows** (2024)
43	
44	This means the benchmark primarily reflects macOS + Chrome performance characteristics.
45

47	
48	1. **Compare within the same Chrome version.** Methodology and throttling differ across releases.
49	2. **Consult the latest run** (currently Chrome 146) for the most up-to-date framework standings.
50	3. **Understand keyed vs non-keyed modes.** Recent odd-numbered Chrome runs benchmark keyed frameworks only, while even-numbered runs include both.
51	4. **60+ data points over 8 years** make this the longest-running, most comprehensive JS framework performance tracker available.
52	5. **Weighted geometric mean** (since Chrome 118) gives a more balanced overall score than the previous arithmetic approach.

# JS Framework Benchmark: 5 Years of Browser Performance Testing

## Overview

The **JS Framework Benchmark** is the most widely referenced open-source benchmark for comparing JavaScript web frameworks on real-world DOM operations. Maintained by Stefan Krause and hosted on GitHub, it measures operations such as creating 1,000 rows, partial updates, row selection, swapping, removal, and startup time — all inside a real Chrome browser with controlled CPU throttling.

Since its inception, the project has published **over 60 official result sets**, covering Chrome versions from **55 (circa 2017) all the way to 146 (mid-2026)**. Each result set captures dozens of frameworks — both keyed and non-keyed implementations — giving developers a consistent yardstick for performance.

## Methodology Milestones

The benchmark has undergone several important methodology changes that make **cross-version comparisons unreliable**:

| Milestone | Chrome Version | Year | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Weighted Geometric Mean | 118 | 2023 | Overall score switched from arithmetic to weighted geometric mean |
| CPU Throttling Adjustment | 118 | 2023 | Throttling factors recalibrated for more realistic load simulation |
| Measurement Fine-Tuning | 118+ | 2023–present | Ongoing refinements to timing and driver instrumentation |
| Keyed-Only Alternation | 139+ | 2025–2026 | Odd Chrome versions often benchmark keyed frameworks only |

Because of these evolving parameters, the project explicitly warns: *"Comparisons across Chrome versions aren't always safe since the benchmark and its driver are constantly developing."*

## Timeline of Official Runs

The table below summarizes the distribution of official benchmark runs by year:

| Year | Chrome Versions | Number of Runs | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2017–2019 | 55, 58, 62, 69 | 4 | Early era; hosted on stefankrause.net |
| 2020 | 83 – 87 | 5 | Migrated to GitHub Pages |
| 2021 | 88 – 96 | 9 | Steady monthly cadence established |
| 2022 | 97 – 108 | 13 | Includes 2 Windows runs (Chrome 104) |
| 2023 | 109 – 120 | 12 | Major methodology overhaul at Chrome 118 |
| 2024 | 121 – 131 | 12 | Includes 1 Windows run (Chrome 121) |
| 2025 | 132 – 143 | 12 | Most active year; alternating keyed-only runs |
| 2026 | 144 – 146 | 3 (so far) | Latest: Chrome 146 on macOS |

## Platform Coverage

The vast majority of runs — **over 95%** — were executed on **macOS (OSX)**. Only two Windows-specific runs exist:

- **Chrome 104 – Windows** (2022)
- **Chrome 121 – Windows** (2024)

This means the benchmark primarily reflects macOS + Chrome performance characteristics.

## Key Takeaways for Developers

1. **Compare within the same Chrome version.** Methodology and throttling differ across releases.
2. **Consult the latest run** (currently Chrome 146) for the most up-to-date framework standings.
3. **Understand keyed vs non-keyed modes.** Recent odd-numbered Chrome runs benchmark keyed frameworks only, while even-numbered runs include both.
4. **60+ data points over 8 years** make this the longest-running, most comprehensive JS framework performance tracker available.
5. **Weighted geometric mean** (since Chrome 118) gives a more balanced overall score than the previous arithmetic approach.

# JS Framework Benchmark: 5 Years of Browser Performance Testing

## Overview

The **JS Framework Benchmark** is the most widely referenced open-source benchmark for comparing JavaScript web frameworks on real-world DOM operations. Maintained by Stefan Krause and hosted on GitHub, it measures operations such as creating 1,000 rows, partial updates, row selection, swapping, removal, and startup time — all inside a real Chrome browser with controlled CPU throttling.

Since its inception, the project has published **over 60 official result sets**, covering Chrome versions from **55 (circa 2017) all the way to 146 (mid-2026)**. Each result set captures dozens of frameworks — both keyed and non-keyed implementations — giving developers a consistent yardstick for performance.

## Methodology Milestones

The benchmark has undergone several important methodology changes that make **cross-version comparisons unreliable**:

| Milestone | Chrome Version | Year | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Weighted Geometric Mean | 118 | 2023 | Overall score switched from arithmetic to weighted geometric mean |
| CPU Throttling Adjustment | 118 | 2023 | Throttling factors recalibrated for more realistic load simulation |
| Measurement Fine-Tuning | 118+ | 2023–present | Ongoing refinements to timing and driver instrumentation |
| Keyed-Only Alternation | 139+ | 2025–2026 | Odd Chrome versions often benchmark keyed frameworks only |

Because of these evolving parameters, the project explicitly warns: *"Comparisons across Chrome versions aren't always safe since the benchmark and its driver are constantly developing."*

## Timeline of Official Runs

The table below summarizes the distribution of official benchmark runs by year:

| Year | Chrome Versions | Number of Runs | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2017–2019 | 55, 58, 62, 69 | 4 | Early era; hosted on stefankrause.net |
| 2020 | 83 – 87 | 5 | Migrated to GitHub Pages |
| 2021 | 88 – 96 | 9 | Steady monthly cadence established |
| 2022 | 97 – 108 | 13 | Includes 2 Windows runs (Chrome 104) |
| 2023 | 109 – 120 | 12 | Major methodology overhaul at Chrome 118 |
| 2024 | 121 – 131 | 12 | Includes 1 Windows run (Chrome 121) |
| 2025 | 132 – 143 | 12 | Most active year; alternating keyed-only runs |
| 2026 | 144 – 146 | 3 (so far) | Latest: Chrome 146 on macOS |

## Platform Coverage

The vast majority of runs — **over 95%** — were executed on **macOS (OSX)**. Only two Windows-specific runs exist:

- **Chrome 104 – Windows** (2022)
- **Chrome 121 – Windows** (2024)

This means the benchmark primarily reflects macOS + Chrome performance characteristics.

## Key Takeaways for Developers

1. **Compare within the same Chrome version.** Methodology and throttling differ across releases.
2. **Consult the latest run** (currently Chrome 146) for the most up-to-date framework standings.
3. **Understand keyed vs non-keyed modes.** Recent odd-numbered Chrome runs benchmark keyed frameworks only, while even-numbered runs include both.
4. **60+ data points over 8 years** make this the longest-running, most comprehensive JS framework performance tracker available.
5. **Weighted geometric mean** (since Chrome 118) gives a more balanced overall score than the previous arithmetic approach.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate the JS Framework Benchmark poster as a single PNG image."""

FONT_MONO = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSansMono.ttf"
FONT_MONO_BOLD = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSansMono-Bold.ttf"
FONT_SANS = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/liberation/LiberationSans-Regular.ttf"
FONT_SANS_BOLD = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/liberation/LiberationSans-Bold.ttf"

title_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 120)
subtitle_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 52)
section_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 64)
body_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 42)
body_bold_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 42)
small_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 36)
small_bold_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 36)
mono_font = load_font(FONT_MONO, 40)
mono_bold_font = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 42)
mono_small = load_font(FONT_MONO, 34)
hero_font = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 180)
hero_label_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 44)
metric_value_font = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 72)
metric_label_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 34)
timeline_year_font = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 48)
timeline_chrome_font = load_font(FONT_MONO, 32)
timeline_note_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 30)

img = Image.new("RGB", (W, H), BG)
draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img)

MARGIN = 140
CONTENT_W = W - 2 * MARGIN

# --- Helper functions ---
def draw_rounded_rect(x, y, w, h, radius, fill, outline=None, outline_width=2):
    draw.rounded_rectangle([x, y, x + w, y + h], radius=radius, fill=fill, outline=outline, width=outline_width)

def draw_dot_grid(x, y, w, h, spacing=40, color="#161B22"):
    for gx in range(x, x + w, spacing):
        for gy in range(y, y + h, spacing):
            draw.ellipse([gx - 1, gy - 1, gx + 1, gy + 1], fill=color)

def text_width(text, font):
    bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), text, font=font)
    return bbox[2] - bbox[0]

def text_height(text, font):
    bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), text, font=font)
    return bbox[3] - bbox[1]

def draw_centered_text(y, text, font, fill):
    tw = text_width(text, font)
    draw.text(((W - tw) // 2, y), text, font=font, fill=fill)

def draw_hline(y, color=GRID_LINE, width=2):
    draw.line([(MARGIN, y), (W - MARGIN, y)], fill=color, width=width)

# --- Subtle background dot grid ---
draw_dot_grid(0, 0, W, H, spacing=48, color="#161B22")

# ============================================================
# HEADER SECTION
# ============================================================
y = 80

# Thin accent line at top
draw.rectangle([0, 0, W, 6], fill=ACCENT_BLUE)

# Title
draw_centered_text(y, "JS Framework Benchmark", title_font, TEXT_PRIMARY)
y += 150

# Subtitle
draw_centered_text(y, "5 Years of Browser Performance Testing", subtitle_font, TEXT_SECONDARY)
y += 90

# One-liner
one_liner = "Tracking JavaScript framework performance across Chrome 55 → 146"
draw_centered_text(y, one_liner, small_font, TEXT_MUTED)
y += 80

# ============================================================
# HERO METRICS ROW
# ============================================================
hero_y = y
hero_h = 320
draw_rounded_rect(MARGIN, hero_y, CONTENT_W, hero_h, 20, BG_CARD, outline=BORDER)

# Three hero metrics
heroes = [
    ("60+", "Official Runs", ACCENT_BLUE),
    ("55 → 146", "Chrome Versions", ACCENT_TEAL),
    ("~8 Years", "Of Benchmarking", ACCENT_AMBER),
]
hero_cell_w = CONTENT_W // 3
for i, (value, label, color) in enumerate(heroes):
    cx = MARGIN + hero_cell_w * i + hero_cell_w // 2
    # Value
    vw = text_width(value, hero_font)
    draw.text((cx - vw // 2, hero_y + 40), value, font=hero_font, fill=color)
    # Label
    lw = text_width(label, hero_label_font)
    draw.text((cx - lw // 2, hero_y + 240), label, font=hero_label_font, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
    # Divider between cells
    if i < 2:
        div_x = MARGIN + hero_cell_w * (i + 1)
        draw.line([(div_x, hero_y + 40), (div_x, hero_y + hero_h - 40)], fill=BORDER, width=2)

y = hero_y + hero_h + 60

# ============================================================
# SECTION 1: OVERVIEW
# ============================================================
draw_hline(y)
y += 40

# Section heading with accent bar
draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y, MARGIN + 8, y + 60], fill=ACCENT_BLUE)
draw.text((MARGIN + 28, y - 4), "What Is the JS Framework Benchmark?", font=section_font, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
y += 90

overview_lines = [
    "The most widely referenced open-source benchmark for comparing JavaScript",
    "web frameworks on real-world DOM operations. Maintained by Stefan Krause,",
    "it measures creating 1,000 rows, partial updates, row selection, swapping,",
    "removal, and startup time — all inside a real Chrome browser with",
    "controlled CPU throttling.",
]
for line in overview_lines:
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), line, font=body_font, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
    y += 56

y += 50

# ============================================================
# SECTION 2: TIMELINE (CENTERPIECE)
# ============================================================
draw_hline(y)
y += 40

draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y, MARGIN + 8, y + 60], fill=ACCENT_TEAL)
draw.text((MARGIN + 28, y - 4), "Benchmark Timeline: Chrome 55 → Chrome 146", font=section_font, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
y += 100

# Timeline data
timeline_data = [
    {"year": "2017–2019", "chrome": "55, 58, 62, 69", "runs": 4, "notes": "Early era; hosted on stefankrause.net", "highlight": False},
    {"year": "2020", "chrome": "83 – 87", "runs": 5, "notes": "Migrated to GitHub Pages", "highlight": False},
    {"year": "2021", "chrome": "88 – 96", "runs": 9, "notes": "Steady monthly cadence established", "highlight": False},
    {"year": "2022", "chrome": "97 – 108", "runs": 13, "notes": "Includes 2 Windows runs (Chrome 104)", "highlight": False},
    {"year": "2023", "chrome": "109 – 120", "runs": 12, "notes": "Major methodology overhaul at Chrome 118", "highlight": True},
    {"year": "2024", "chrome": "121 – 131", "runs": 12, "notes": "Includes 1 Windows run (Chrome 121)", "highlight": False},
    {"year": "2025", "chrome": "132 – 143", "runs": 12, "notes": "Most active year; alternating keyed-only", "highlight": False},
    {"year": "2026", "chrome": "144 – 146", "runs": 3, "notes": "Latest: Chrome 146 on macOS", "highlight": False},
]

# Timeline as a visual strip
row_h = 110
timeline_x = MARGIN
bar_max_w = 480
max_runs = 13

# Column positions
col_year_x = MARGIN + 20
col_chrome_x = MARGIN + 280
col_bar_x = MARGIN + 620
col_runs_x = col_bar_x + bar_max_w + 30
col_notes_x = col_runs_x + 110

# Header row
draw.text((col_year_x, y), "YEAR", font=small_bold_font, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
draw.text((col_chrome_x, y), "CHROME", font=small_bold_font, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
draw.text((col_bar_x, y), "RUNS", font=small_bold_font, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
draw.text((col_notes_x, y), "NOTES", font=small_bold_font, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
y += 60

for entry in timeline_data:
    row_bg = HIGHLIGHT_BG if entry["highlight"] else None
    if row_bg:
        draw_rounded_rect(MARGIN, y - 10, CONTENT_W, row_h, 12, row_bg, outline=ACCENT_AMBER, outline_width=2)

    # Year
    year_color = ACCENT_AMBER if entry["highlight"] else ACCENT_BLUE
    draw.text((col_year_x, y + 18), entry["year"], font=timeline_year_font, fill=year_color)

    # Chrome versions
    draw.text((col_chrome_x, y + 26), entry["chrome"], font=timeline_chrome_font, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)

    # Bar
    bar_w = int((entry["runs"] / max_runs) * bar_max_w)
    bar_color = ACCENT_AMBER if entry["highlight"] else ACCENT_TEAL
    bar_y = y + 28
    bar_h = 36
    draw_rounded_rect(col_bar_x, bar_y, bar_w, bar_h, 6, bar_color)

    # Run count
    draw.text((col_runs_x, y + 22), str(entry["runs"]), font=mono_bold_font, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)

    # Notes
    note_color = ACCENT_AMBER if entry["highlight"] else TEXT_MUTED
    draw.text((col_notes_x, y + 28), entry["notes"], font=timeline_note_font, fill=note_color)

    y += row_h

y += 40

# ============================================================
# CAUTION CALLOUT — Chrome 118 methodology change
# ============================================================
caution_h = 200
draw_rounded_rect(MARGIN, y, CONTENT_W, caution_h, 16, "#2D1F00", outline=ACCENT_AMBER, outline_width=3)

# Warning icon (triangle with !)
tri_x = MARGIN + 40
tri_y = y + caution_h // 2
tri_size = 36
draw.polygon([
    (tri_x, tri_y - tri_size),
    (tri_x - tri_size, tri_y + tri_size),
    (tri_x + tri_size, tri_y + tri_size),
], fill=ACCENT_AMBER)

y += caution_h + 60

y += 40

draw.text((MARGIN + 28, y - 4), "Methodology Milestones", font=section_font, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
y += 100

milestones = [

    ("Chrome 118+", "2023–now", "Measurement Fine-Tuning", "Ongoing refinements to timing and driver instrumentation", ACCENT_TEAL),
    ("Chrome 139+", "2025–26", "Keyed-Only Alternation", "Odd Chrome versions often benchmark keyed frameworks only", ACCENT_BLUE),
]

card_h = 140
card_gap = 20
cards_per_row = 2
card_w = (CONTENT_W - card_gap) // cards_per_row

    row = i // cards_per_row
    cx = MARGIN + col * (card_w + card_gap)
    cy = y + row * (card_h + card_gap)

    draw_rounded_rect(cx, cy, card_w, card_h, 12, BG_CARD, outline=BORDER)
    # Color accent on left
    draw.rectangle([cx, cy, cx + 6, cy + card_h], fill=color)

    # Chrome version badge

    bw = text_width(badge_text, mono_small) + 20
    draw_rounded_rect(cx + 30, cy + 18, bw, 38, 8, color + "22")

    # Title
    draw.text((cx + 30, cy + 66), title, font=body_bold_font, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)

    # Description
    draw.text((cx + 30, cy + 112), desc[:65], font=small_font, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)

y += (card_h + card_gap) * 2 + 50

# ============================================================

y += 40

y += 100

# Left: Platform card
plat_h = 340
draw_rounded_rect(MARGIN, y, left_w, plat_h, 16, BG_CARD, outline=BORDER)

draw.text((MARGIN + 40, y + 30), "PRIMARY PLATFORM", font=small_bold_font, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
draw.text((MARGIN + 40, y + 80), "macOS (OSX)", font=metric_value_font, fill=ACCENT_TEAL)
draw.text((MARGIN + 40, y + 170), "95%+ of all runs on macOS + Chrome", font=small_font, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)

# Mini bar: macOS vs Windows
bar_total_w = left_w - 80
macos_bar_w = int(bar_total_w * 0.97)
win_bar_w = bar_total_w - macos_bar_w
bar_y2 = y + 230
draw_rounded_rect(MARGIN + 40, bar_y2, macos_bar_w, 36, 6, ACCENT_TEAL)
draw_rounded_rect(MARGIN + 40 + macos_bar_w + 4, bar_y2, win_bar_w, 36, 6, ACCENT_BLUE)
draw.text((MARGIN + 40, bar_y2 + 48), "macOS: 58+ runs", font=small_font, fill=ACCENT_TEAL)
draw.text((MARGIN + 40 + macos_bar_w - 260, bar_y2 + 48), "Windows: 2 runs", font=small_font, fill=ACCENT_BLUE)

# Right: Key metrics grid
right_x = MARGIN + left_w + 40
draw_rounded_rect(right_x, y, right_w, plat_h, 16, BG_CARD, outline=BORDER)

metrics = [
    ("12", "Runs in 2025", "Most active year"),
    ("Chrome 146", "Latest Run", "macOS, mid-2026"),
    ("2", "Windows Runs", "Chrome 104 & 121"),
    ("Keyed vs Non", "Framework Modes", "Alternating since v139"),
]

met_cols = 2
met_rows = 2
met_w = (right_w - 40) // met_cols
met_h = (plat_h - 40) // met_rows

for i, (val, label, ctx) in enumerate(metrics):
    mc = i % met_cols
    mr = i // met_cols
    mx = right_x + 20 + mc * met_w
    my = y + 20 + mr * met_h

    val_color = [ACCENT_BLUE, ACCENT_TEAL, ACCENT_AMBER, ACCENT_BLUE][i]
    val_font = metric_value_font if len(val) <= 4 else load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 52)
    draw.text((mx + 10, my + 5), val, font=val_font, fill=val_color)

# ============================================================
draw_hline(y)
y += 40

draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y, MARGIN + 8, y + 60], fill=ACCENT_TEAL)
draw.text((MARGIN + 28, y - 4), "Key Takeaways for Developers", font=section_font, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
y += 100

takeaways = [
    ("1", "Compare within the same Chrome version.", "Methodology and throttling differ across releases."),
    ("2", "Consult the latest run (Chrome 146)", "for the most up-to-date framework standings."),
    ("3", "Understand keyed vs non-keyed modes.", "Recent odd-numbered Chrome runs = keyed only."),
    ("4", "60+ data points over ~8 years", "make this the most comprehensive JS perf tracker."),
    ("5", "Weighted geometric mean since Chrome 118", "gives a more balanced overall score than arithmetic."),

takeaway_h = 90
for num, main, sub in takeaways:
    # Number circle
    circle_x = MARGIN + 40
    circle_y = y + takeaway_h // 2
    circle_r = 30
    draw.ellipse([circle_x - circle_r, circle_y - circle_r, circle_x + circle_r, circle_y + circle_r], fill=ACCENT_TEAL + "33", outline=ACCENT_TEAL, width=2)
    nw = text_width(num, takeaway_num_font)
    draw.text((circle_x - nw // 2, circle_y - 28), num, font=takeaway_num_font, fill=ACCENT_TEAL)

    # Text
    draw.text((MARGIN + 110, y + 10), main, font=body_bold_font, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
    draw.text((MARGIN + 110, y + 56), sub, font=body_font, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)

    y += takeaway_h

y += 40

# ============================================================
# FOOTER
# ============================================================
draw_hline(y)
y += 30

footer_text = "Data: github.com/nickvdp/js-framework-benchmark  •  Generated April 2026  •  Dark-mode poster"
fw = text_width(footer_text, small_font)
draw.text(((W - fw) // 2, y), footer_text, font=small_font, fill=TEXT_MUTED)

# Bottom accent line
draw.rectangle([0, H - 6, W, H], fill=ACCENT_BLUE)

# --- Save ---
os.makedirs("/app/output", exist_ok=True)
img.save("/app/output/final_poster.png", "PNG", dpi=(150, 150))
print(f"Poster saved: /app/output/final_poster.png ({W}x{H}px)")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate the JS Framework Benchmark poster as a single PNG image."""

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
import math
import os

# --- Dimensions: A1 portrait at 150 DPI ---
W, H = 3508, 4961

# --- Color palette: dark-mode developer aesthetic ---
BG = "#0D1117"
BG_CARD = "#161B22"
BG_CARD_ALT = "#1C2333"
ACCENT_BLUE = "#58A6FF"
ACCENT_TEAL = "#3FB9A0"
ACCENT_AMBER = "#F0B429"
ACCENT_RED = "#F87171"
TEXT_PRIMARY = "#E6EDF3"
TEXT_SECONDARY = "#8B949E"
TEXT_MUTED = "#6E7681"
GRID_LINE = "#21262D"
BORDER = "#30363D"
HIGHLIGHT_BG = "#1A1F2E"

# --- Fonts ---
def load_font(path, size):
    try:
        return ImageFont.truetype(path, size)
    except:
        return ImageFont.load_default()

FONT_MONO = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSansMono.ttf"
FONT_MONO_BOLD = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSansMono-Bold.ttf"
FONT_SANS = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/liberation/LiberationSans-Regular.ttf"
FONT_SANS_BOLD = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/liberation/LiberationSans-Bold.ttf"

title_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 120)
subtitle_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 52)
section_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 64)
body_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 42)
body_bold_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 42)
small_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 36)
small_bold_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 36)
mono_font = load_font(FONT_MONO, 40)
mono_bold_font = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 42)
mono_small = load_font(FONT_MONO, 34)
hero_font = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 180)
hero_label_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 44)
metric_value_font = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 72)
metric_label_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 34)
timeline_year_font = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 48)
timeline_chrome_font = load_font(FONT_MONO, 32)
timeline_note_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 30)
takeaway_num_font = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 56)
takeaway_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 38)
warning_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 44)
caution_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 38)

img = Image.new("RGB", (W, H), BG)
draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img)

MARGIN = 140
CONTENT_W = W - 2 * MARGIN

# --- Helper functions ---
def draw_rounded_rect(x, y, w, h, radius, fill, outline=None, outline_width=2):
    draw.rounded_rectangle([x, y, x + w, y + h], radius=radius, fill=fill, outline=outline, width=outline_width)

def draw_dot_grid(x, y, w, h, spacing=40, color="#161B22"):
    for gx in range(x, x + w, spacing):
        for gy in range(y, y + h, spacing):
            draw.ellipse([gx - 1, gy - 1, gx + 1, gy + 1], fill=color)

def text_width(text, font):
    bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), text, font=font)
    return bbox[2] - bbox[0]

def text_height(text, font):
    bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), text, font=font)
    return bbox[3] - bbox[1]

def draw_centered_text(y, text, font, fill):
    tw = text_width(text, font)
    draw.text(((W - tw) // 2, y), text, font=font, fill=fill)

def draw_hline(y, color=GRID_LINE, width=2):
    draw.line([(MARGIN, y), (W - MARGIN, y)], fill=color, width=width)

# --- Subtle background dot grid ---
draw_dot_grid(0, 0, W, H, spacing=48, color="#161B22")

# ============================================================
# HEADER SECTION
# ============================================================
y = 80

# Thin accent line at top
draw.rectangle([0, 0, W, 6], fill=ACCENT_BLUE)

# Title
draw_centered_text(y, "JS Framework Benchmark", title_font, TEXT_PRIMARY)
y += 150

# Subtitle
draw_centered_text(y, "5 Years of Browser Performance Testing", subtitle_font, TEXT_SECONDARY)
y += 90

# One-liner
one_liner = "Tracking JavaScript framework performance across Chrome 55 → 146"
draw_centered_text(y, one_liner, small_font, TEXT_MUTED)
y += 80

# ============================================================
# HERO METRICS ROW
# ============================================================
hero_y = y
hero_h = 320
draw_rounded_rect(MARGIN, hero_y, CONTENT_W, hero_h, 20, BG_CARD, outline=BORDER)

# Three hero metrics
heroes = [
    ("60+", "Official Runs", ACCENT_BLUE),
    ("55 → 146", "Chrome Versions", ACCENT_TEAL),
    ("~8 Years", "Of Benchmarking", ACCENT_AMBER),
]
hero_cell_w = CONTENT_W // 3
for i, (value, label, color) in enumerate(heroes):
    cx = MARGIN + hero_cell_w * i + hero_cell_w // 2
    # Value
    vw = text_width(value, hero_font)
    draw.text((cx - vw // 2, hero_y + 40), value, font=hero_font, fill=color)
    # Label
    lw = text_width(label, hero_label_font)
    draw.text((cx - lw // 2, hero_y + 240), label, font=hero_label_font, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
    # Divider between cells
    if i < 2:
        div_x = MARGIN + hero_cell_w * (i + 1)
        draw.line([(div_x, hero_y + 40), (div_x, hero_y + hero_h - 40)], fill=BORDER, width=2)

y = hero_y + hero_h + 60

# ============================================================
# SECTION 1: OVERVIEW
# ============================================================
draw_hline(y)
y += 40

# Section heading with accent bar
draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y, MARGIN + 8, y + 60], fill=ACCENT_BLUE)
draw.text((MARGIN + 28, y - 4), "What Is the JS Framework Benchmark?", font=section_font, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
y += 90

overview_lines = [
    "The most widely referenced open-source benchmark for comparing JavaScript",
    "web frameworks on real-world DOM operations. Maintained by Stefan Krause,",
    "it measures creating 1,000 rows, partial updates, row selection, swapping,",
    "removal, and startup time — all inside a real Chrome browser with",
    "controlled CPU throttling.",
]
for line in overview_lines:
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), line, font=body_font, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
    y += 56

y += 50

# SECTION 2: TIMELINE (CENTERPIECE)
# ============================================================
draw_hline(y)
y += 40

draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y, MARGIN + 8, y + 60], fill=ACCENT_TEAL)
draw.text((MARGIN + 28, y - 4), "Benchmark Timeline: Chrome 55 → Chrome 146", font=section_font, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
y += 100

# Timeline data
timeline_data = [
    {"year": "2017–2019", "chrome": "55, 58, 62, 69", "runs": 4, "notes": "Early era; hosted on stefankrause.net", "highlight": False},
    {"year": "2020", "chrome": "83 – 87", "runs": 5, "notes": "Migrated to GitHub Pages", "highlight": False},
    {"year": "2021", "chrome": "88 – 96", "runs": 9, "notes": "Steady monthly cadence established", "highlight": False},
    {"year": "2022", "chrome": "97 – 108", "runs": 13, "notes": "Includes 2 Windows runs (Chrome 104)", "highlight": False},
    {"year": "2023", "chrome": "109 – 120", "runs": 12, "notes": "Major methodology overhaul at Chrome 118", "highlight": True},
    {"year": "2024", "chrome": "121 – 131", "runs": 12, "notes": "Includes 1 Windows run (Chrome 121)", "highlight": False},
    {"year": "2025", "chrome": "132 – 143", "runs": 12, "notes": "Most active year; alternating keyed-only", "highlight": False},
    {"year": "2026", "chrome": "144 – 146", "runs": 3, "notes": "Latest: Chrome 146 on macOS", "highlight": False},
]

# Timeline as a visual strip
row_h = 110
timeline_x = MARGIN
bar_max_w = 480
max_runs = 13

# Column positions
col_year_x = MARGIN + 20
col_chrome_x = MARGIN + 280
col_bar_x = MARGIN + 620
col_runs_x = col_bar_x + bar_max_w + 30
col_notes_x = col_runs_x + 110

# Header row
draw.text((col_year_x, y), "YEAR", font=small_bold_font, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
draw.text((col_chrome_x, y), "CHROME", font=small_bold_font, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
draw.text((col_bar_x, y), "RUNS", font=small_bold_font, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
draw.text((col_notes_x, y), "NOTES", font=small_bold_font, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
y += 60

for entry in timeline_data:
    row_bg = HIGHLIGHT_BG if entry["highlight"] else None
    if row_bg:
        draw_rounded_rect(MARGIN, y - 10, CONTENT_W, row_h, 12, row_bg, outline=ACCENT_AMBER, outline_width=2)

    # Year
    year_color = ACCENT_AMBER if entry["highlight"] else ACCENT_BLUE
    draw.text((col_year_x, y + 18), entry["year"], font=timeline_year_font, fill=year_color)

    # Chrome versions
    draw.text((col_chrome_x, y + 26), entry["chrome"], font=timeline_chrome_font, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)

    # Bar
    bar_w = int((entry["runs"] / max_runs) * bar_max_w)
    bar_color = ACCENT_AMBER if entry["highlight"] else ACCENT_TEAL
    bar_y = y + 28
    bar_h = 36
    draw_rounded_rect(col_bar_x, bar_y, bar_w, bar_h, 6, bar_color)

    # Run count
    draw.text((col_runs_x, y + 22), str(entry["runs"]), font=mono_bold_font, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)

    # Notes
    note_color = ACCENT_AMBER if entry["highlight"] else TEXT_MUTED
    draw.text((col_notes_x, y + 28), entry["notes"], font=timeline_note_font, fill=note_color)

    y += row_h

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate the JS Framework Benchmark poster as a single PNG image."""

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
import math
import os

# --- Dimensions: A1 portrait at 150 DPI ---
W, H = 3508, 4961

# --- Color palette: dark-mode developer aesthetic ---
BG = "#0D1117"
BG_CARD = "#161B22"
BG_CARD_ALT = "#1C2333"
ACCENT_BLUE = "#58A6FF"
ACCENT_TEAL = "#3FB9A0"
ACCENT_AMBER = "#F0B429"
ACCENT_RED = "#F87171"
TEXT_PRIMARY = "#E6EDF3"
TEXT_SECONDARY = "#8B949E"
TEXT_MUTED = "#6E7681"
GRID_LINE = "#21262D"
BORDER = "#30363D"
HIGHLIGHT_BG = "#1A1F2E"

# --- Fonts ---
def load_font(path, size):
    try:
        return ImageFont.truetype(path, size)
    except:
        return ImageFont.load_default()

FONT_MONO = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSansMono.ttf"
FONT_MONO_BOLD = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSansMono-Bold.ttf"
FONT_SANS = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/liberation/LiberationSans-Regular.ttf"
FONT_SANS_BOLD = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/liberation/LiberationSans-Bold.ttf"

title_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 120)
subtitle_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 52)
section_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 64)
body_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 42)
body_bold_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 42)
small_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 36)
small_bold_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 36)
mono_font = load_font(FONT_MONO, 40)
mono_bold_font = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 42)
mono_small = load_font(FONT_MONO, 34)
hero_font = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 180)
hero_label_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 44)
metric_value_font = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 72)
metric_label_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 34)
timeline_year_font = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 48)
timeline_chrome_font = load_font(FONT_MONO, 32)
timeline_note_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 30)
takeaway_num_font = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 56)
takeaway_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 38)
warning_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 44)
caution_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 38)

img = Image.new("RGB", (W, H), BG)
draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img)

MARGIN = 140
CONTENT_W = W - 2 * MARGIN

# --- Helper functions ---
def draw_rounded_rect(x, y, w, h, radius, fill, outline=None, outline_width=2):
    draw.rounded_rectangle([x, y, x + w, y + h], radius=radius, fill=fill, outline=outline, width=outline_width)

def draw_dot_grid(x, y, w, h, spacing=40, color="#161B22"):
    for gx in range(x, x + w, spacing):
        for gy in range(y, y + h, spacing):
            draw.ellipse([gx - 1, gy - 1, gx + 1, gy + 1], fill=color)

def text_width(text, font):
    bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), text, font=font)
    return bbox[2] - bbox[0]

def text_height(text, font):
    bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), text, font=font)
    return bbox[3] - bbox[1]

def draw_centered_text(y, text, font, fill):
    tw = text_width(text, font)
    draw.text(((W - tw) // 2, y), text, font=font, fill=fill)

def draw_hline(y, color=GRID_LINE, width=2):
    draw.line([(MARGIN, y), (W - MARGIN, y)], fill=color, width=width)

# --- Subtle background dot grid ---
draw_dot_grid(0, 0, W, H, spacing=48, color="#161B22")

# ============================================================
# HEADER SECTION
# ============================================================
y = 80

# Thin accent line at top
draw.rectangle([0, 0, W, 6], fill=ACCENT_BLUE)

# Title
draw_centered_text(y, "JS Framework Benchmark", title_font, TEXT_PRIMARY)
y += 150

# Subtitle
draw_centered_text(y, "5 Years of Browser Performance Testing", subtitle_font, TEXT_SECONDARY)
y += 90

# One-liner
one_liner = "Tracking JavaScript framework performance across Chrome 55 → 146"
draw_centered_text(y, one_liner, small_font, TEXT_MUTED)
y += 80

# ============================================================
# HERO METRICS ROW
# ============================================================
hero_y = y
hero_h = 320
draw_rounded_rect(MARGIN, hero_y, CONTENT_W, hero_h, 20, BG_CARD, outline=BORDER)

# Three hero metrics
heroes = [
    ("60+", "Official Runs", ACCENT_BLUE),
    ("55 → 146", "Chrome Versions", ACCENT_TEAL),
    ("~8 Years", "Of Benchmarking", ACCENT_AMBER),
]
hero_cell_w = CONTENT_W // 3
for i, (value, label, color) in enumerate(heroes):
    cx = MARGIN + hero_cell_w * i + hero_cell_w // 2
    # Value
    vw = text_width(value, hero_font)
    draw.text((cx - vw // 2, hero_y + 40), value, font=hero_font, fill=color)
    # Label
    lw = text_width(label, hero_label_font)
    draw.text((cx - lw // 2, hero_y + 240), label, font=hero_label_font, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
    # Divider between cells
    if i < 2:
        div_x = MARGIN + hero_cell_w * (i + 1)
        draw.line([(div_x, hero_y + 40), (div_x, hero_y + hero_h - 40)], fill=BORDER, width=2)

y = hero_y + hero_h + 60

# ============================================================
# SECTION 1: OVERVIEW
# ============================================================
draw_hline(y)
y += 40

# Section heading with accent bar
draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y, MARGIN + 8, y + 60], fill=ACCENT_BLUE)
draw.text((MARGIN + 28, y - 4), "What Is the JS Framework Benchmark?", font=section_font, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
y += 90

overview_lines = [
    "The most widely referenced open-source benchmark for comparing JavaScript",
    "web frameworks on real-world DOM operations. Maintained by Stefan Krause,",
    "it measures creating 1,000 rows, partial updates, row selection, swapping,",
    "removal, and startup time — all inside a real Chrome browser with",
    "controlled CPU throttling.",
]
for line in overview_lines:
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), line, font=body_font, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
    y += 56

y += 50

# ============================================================
# SECTION 2: TIMELINE (CENTERPIECE)
# ============================================================
draw_hline(y)
y += 40

draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y, MARGIN + 8, y + 60], fill=ACCENT_TEAL)
draw.text((MARGIN + 28, y - 4), "Benchmark Timeline: Chrome 55 → Chrome 146", font=section_font, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
y += 100

# Timeline data
timeline_data = [
    {"year": "2017–2019", "chrome": "55, 58, 62, 69", "runs": 4, "notes": "Early era; hosted on stefankrause.net", "highlight": False},
    {"year": "2020", "chrome": "83 – 87", "runs": 5, "notes": "Migrated to GitHub Pages", "highlight": False},
    {"year": "2021", "chrome": "88 – 96", "runs": 9, "notes": "Steady monthly cadence established", "highlight": False},
    {"year": "2022", "chrome": "97 – 108", "runs": 13, "notes": "Includes 2 Windows runs (Chrome 104)", "highlight": False},
    {"year": "2023", "chrome": "109 – 120", "runs": 12, "notes": "Major methodology overhaul at Chrome 118", "highlight": True},
    {"year": "2024", "chrome": "121 – 131", "runs": 12, "notes": "Includes 1 Windows run (Chrome 121)", "highlight": False},
    {"year": "2025", "chrome": "132 – 143", "runs": 12, "notes": "Most active year; alternating keyed-only", "highlight": False},
    {"year": "2026", "chrome": "144 – 146", "runs": 3, "notes": "Latest: Chrome 146 on macOS", "highlight": False},
]

# Timeline as a visual strip
row_h = 110
timeline_x = MARGIN
bar_max_w = 480
max_runs = 13

# Column positions
col_year_x = MARGIN + 20
col_chrome_x = MARGIN + 280
col_bar_x = MARGIN + 620
col_runs_x = col_bar_x + bar_max_w + 30
col_notes_x = col_runs_x + 110

# Header row
draw.text((col_year_x, y), "YEAR", font=small_bold_font, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
draw.text((col_chrome_x, y), "CHROME", font=small_bold_font, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
draw.text((col_bar_x, y), "RUNS", font=small_bold_font, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
draw.text((col_notes_x, y), "NOTES", font=small_bold_font, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
y += 60

for entry in timeline_data:
    row_bg = HIGHLIGHT_BG if entry["highlight"] else None
    if row_bg:
        draw_rounded_rect(MARGIN, y - 10, CONTENT_W, row_h, 12, row_bg, outline=ACCENT_AMBER, outline_width=2)

    # Year
    year_color = ACCENT_AMBER if entry["highlight"] else ACCENT_BLUE
    draw.text((col_year_x, y + 18), entry["year"], font=timeline_year_font, fill=year_color)

    # Chrome versions
    draw.text((col_chrome_x, y + 26), entry["chrome"], font=timeline_chrome_font, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)

    # Bar
    bar_w = int((entry["runs"] / max_runs) * bar_max_w)
    bar_color = ACCENT_AMBER if entry["highlight"] else ACCENT_TEAL
    bar_y = y + 28
    bar_h = 36
    draw_rounded_rect(col_bar_x, bar_y, bar_w, bar_h, 6, bar_color)

    # Run count
    draw.text((col_runs_x, y + 22), str(entry["runs"]), font=mono_bold_font, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)

    # Notes
    note_color = ACCENT_AMBER if entry["highlight"] else TEXT_MUTED
    draw.text((col_notes_x, y + 28), entry["notes"], font=timeline_note_font, fill=note_color)

    y += row_h

y += 40

# ============================================================
# CAUTION CALLOUT — Chrome 118 methodology change
# ============================================================
caution_h = 200
draw_rounded_rect(MARGIN, y, CONTENT_W, caution_h, 16, "#2D1F00", outline=ACCENT_AMBER, outline_width=3)

# Warning icon (triangle with !)
tri_x = MARGIN + 40
tri_y = y + caution_h // 2
tri_size = 36
draw.polygon([
    (tri_x, tri_y - tri_size),
    (tri_x - tri_size, tri_y + tri_size),
    (tri_x + tri_size, tri_y + tri_size),
], fill=ACCENT_AMBER)
draw.text((tri_x - 8, tri_y - 18), "!", font=load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 40), fill="#2D1F00")

draw.text((MARGIN + 110, y + 30), "⚠  METHODOLOGY BREAK AT CHROME 118", font=warning_font, fill=ACCENT_AMBER)
caution_lines = [
    "Scoring switched from arithmetic mean to weighted geometric mean. CPU throttling was",
    "recalibrated. Cross-version comparisons before and after Chrome 118 are unreliable.",
]
cy = y + 90
for line in caution_lines:
    draw.text((MARGIN + 110, cy), line, font=caution_font, fill="#F0D68A")
    cy += 48

y += caution_h + 60

# ============================================================
# SECTION 3: METHODOLOGY MILESTONES
# ============================================================
draw_hline(y)
y += 40

draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y, MARGIN + 8, y + 60], fill=ACCENT_AMBER)
draw.text((MARGIN + 28, y - 4), "Methodology Milestones", font=section_font, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
y += 100

milestones = [
    ("Chrome 118", "2023", "Weighted Geometric Mean", "Overall score switched from arithmetic to weighted geometric mean", ACCENT_AMBER),
    ("Chrome 118", "2023", "CPU Throttling Adjustment", "Throttling factors recalibrated for more realistic load simulation", ACCENT_AMBER),
    ("Chrome 118+", "2023–now", "Measurement Fine-Tuning", "Ongoing refinements to timing and driver instrumentation", ACCENT_TEAL),
    ("Chrome 139+", "2025–26", "Keyed-Only Alternation", "Odd Chrome versions often benchmark keyed frameworks only", ACCENT_BLUE),
]

card_h = 140
card_gap = 20
cards_per_row = 2
card_w = (CONTENT_W - card_gap) // cards_per_row

for i, (chrome, year, title, desc, color) in enumerate(milestones):
    col = i % cards_per_row
    row = i // cards_per_row
    cx = MARGIN + col * (card_w + card_gap)
    cy = y + row * (card_h + card_gap)

    draw_rounded_rect(cx, cy, card_w, card_h, 12, BG_CARD, outline=BORDER)
    # Color accent on left
    draw.rectangle([cx, cy, cx + 6, cy + card_h], fill=color)

    # Chrome version badge
    badge_text = chrome
    bw = text_width(badge_text, mono_small) + 20
    draw_rounded_rect(cx + 30, cy + 18, bw, 38, 8, color + "22")
    draw.text((cx + 40, cy + 20), badge_text, font=mono_small, fill=color)

    # Year
    draw.text((cx + 50 + bw, cy + 22), year, font=small_font, fill=TEXT_MUTED)

    # Title
    draw.text((cx + 30, cy + 66), title, font=body_bold_font, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)

    # Description
    draw.text((cx + 30, cy + 112), desc[:65], font=small_font, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)

y += (card_h + card_gap) * 2 + 50

# ============================================================
# SECTION 4: PLATFORM & COVERAGE
# ============================================================
draw_hline(y)
y += 40

draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y, MARGIN + 8, y + 60], fill=ACCENT_BLUE)
draw.text((MARGIN + 28, y - 4), "Platform & Framework Coverage", font=section_font, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
y += 100

# Two-column layout: platform stat + metrics
left_w = CONTENT_W // 2 - 20
right_w = CONTENT_W // 2 - 20

# Left: Platform card
plat_h = 340
draw_rounded_rect(MARGIN, y, left_w, plat_h, 16, BG_CARD, outline=BORDER)

draw.text((MARGIN + 40, y + 30), "PRIMARY PLATFORM", font=small_bold_font, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
draw.text((MARGIN + 40, y + 80), "macOS (OSX)", font=metric_value_font, fill=ACCENT_TEAL)
draw.text((MARGIN + 40, y + 170), "95%+ of all runs on macOS + Chrome", font=small_font, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)

# Mini bar: macOS vs Windows
bar_total_w = left_w - 80
macos_bar_w = int(bar_total_w * 0.97)
win_bar_w = bar_total_w - macos_bar_w
bar_y2 = y + 230
draw_rounded_rect(MARGIN + 40, bar_y2, macos_bar_w, 36, 6, ACCENT_TEAL)
draw_rounded_rect(MARGIN + 40 + macos_bar_w + 4, bar_y2, win_bar_w, 36, 6, ACCENT_BLUE)
draw.text((MARGIN + 40, bar_y2 + 48), "macOS: 58+ runs", font=small_font, fill=ACCENT_TEAL)
draw.text((MARGIN + 40 + macos_bar_w - 260, bar_y2 + 48), "Windows: 2 runs", font=small_font, fill=ACCENT_BLUE)

# Right: Key metrics grid
right_x = MARGIN + left_w + 40
draw_rounded_rect(right_x, y, right_w, plat_h, 16, BG_CARD, outline=BORDER)

metrics = [
    ("12", "Runs in 2025", "Most active year"),
    ("Chrome 146", "Latest Run", "macOS, mid-2026"),
    ("2", "Windows Runs", "Chrome 104 & 121"),
    ("Keyed vs Non", "Framework Modes", "Alternating since v139"),
]

met_cols = 2
met_rows = 2
met_w = (right_w - 40) // met_cols
met_h = (plat_h - 40) // met_rows

for i, (val, label, ctx) in enumerate(metrics):
    mc = i % met_cols
    mr = i // met_cols
    mx = right_x + 20 + mc * met_w
    my = y + 20 + mr * met_h

    val_color = [ACCENT_BLUE, ACCENT_TEAL, ACCENT_AMBER, ACCENT_BLUE][i]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate the JS Framework Benchmark poster as a single PNG image."""

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
import os

# --- Dimensions: A1 portrait at 150 DPI ---
W, H = 3508, 4961

# --- Color palette: dark-mode developer aesthetic ---
BG = "#0D1117"
BG_CARD = "#161B22"
BG_CARD_ALT = "#1C2333"
ACCENT_BLUE = "#58A6FF"
ACCENT_TEAL = "#3FB9A0"
ACCENT_AMBER = "#F0B429"
TEXT_PRIMARY = "#E6EDF3"
TEXT_SECONDARY = "#8B949E"
TEXT_MUTED = "#6E7681"
GRID_LINE = "#21262D"
BORDER = "#30363D"
HIGHLIGHT_BG = "#1A1F2E"

# --- Fonts ---
def load_font(path, size):
    try:
        return ImageFont.truetype(path, size)
    except:
        return ImageFont.load_default()

FONT_MONO = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSansMono.ttf"
FONT_MONO_BOLD = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSansMono-Bold.ttf"
FONT_SANS = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/liberation/LiberationSans-Regular.ttf"
FONT_SANS_BOLD = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/liberation/LiberationSans-Bold.ttf"

title_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 130)
subtitle_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 58)
section_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 68)
body_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 44)
body_bold_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 44)
small_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 38)
small_bold_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 38)
mono_small = load_font(FONT_MONO, 36)
mono_bold_font = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 44)
hero_font = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 190)
hero_label_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 48)
metric_value_font = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 76)
timeline_year_font = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 50)
timeline_chrome_font = load_font(FONT_MONO, 36)
timeline_note_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 34)
takeaway_num_font = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 58)
warning_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 48)
caution_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 40)

img = Image.new("RGB", (W, H), BG)
draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img)

MARGIN = 140
CONTENT_W = W - 2 * MARGIN

# --- Helper functions ---

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate the JS Framework Benchmark poster as a single PNG image."""

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
import os

# --- Dimensions: A1 portrait at 150 DPI ---
W, H = 3508, 4961

# --- Color palette: dark-mode developer aesthetic ---
BG = "#0D1117"
BG_CARD = "#161B22"
BG_CARD_ALT = "#1C2333"
ACCENT_BLUE = "#58A6FF"
ACCENT_TEAL = "#3FB9A0"
ACCENT_AMBER = "#F0B429"
TEXT_PRIMARY = "#E6EDF3"
TEXT_SECONDARY = "#8B949E"
TEXT_MUTED = "#6E7681"
GRID_LINE = "#21262D"
BORDER = "#30363D"
HIGHLIGHT_BG = "#1A1F2E"

# --- Fonts ---
def load_font(path, size):
    try:
        return ImageFont.truetype(path, size)
    except:
        return ImageFont.load_default()

FONT_MONO = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSansMono.ttf"
FONT_MONO_BOLD = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSansMono-Bold.ttf"
FONT_SANS = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/liberation/LiberationSans-Regular.ttf"
FONT_SANS_BOLD = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/liberation/LiberationSans-Bold.ttf"

title_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 130)
subtitle_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 58)
section_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 68)
body_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 44)
body_bold_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 44)
small_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 38)
small_bold_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 38)
mono_small = load_font(FONT_MONO, 36)
mono_bold_font = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 44)
hero_font = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 190)
hero_label_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 48)
metric_value_font = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 76)
timeline_year_font = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 50)
timeline_chrome_font = load_font(FONT_MONO, 36)
timeline_note_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 34)
takeaway_num_font = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 58)
warning_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 48)
caution_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 40)

img = Image.new("RGB", (W, H), BG)
draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img)

MARGIN = 140
CONTENT_W = W - 2 * MARGIN

# --- Helper functions ---
def draw_rounded_rect(x, y, w, h, radius, fill, outline=None, outline_width=2):
    draw.rounded_rectangle([x, y, x + w, y + h], radius=radius, fill=fill, outline=outline, width=outline_width)

def draw_dot_grid(x, y, w, h, spacing=40, color="#161B22"):
    for gx in range(x, x + w, spacing):
        for gy in range(y, y + h, spacing):
            draw.ellipse([gx - 1, gy - 1, gx + 1, gy + 1], fill=color)

def text_width(text, font):
    bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), text, font=font)
    return bbox[2] - bbox[0]

def draw_centered_text(y, text, font, fill):
    tw = text_width(text, font)
    draw.text(((W - tw) // 2, y), text, font=font, fill=fill)

def draw_hline(y, color=GRID_LINE, width=2):
    draw.line([(MARGIN, y), (W - MARGIN, y)], fill=color, width=width)

# --- Subtle background dot grid ---
draw_dot_grid(0, 0, W, H, spacing=48, color="#161B22")

# ============================================================
# HEADER SECTION
# ============================================================
y = 100

# Accent line top
draw.rectangle([0, 0, W, 8], fill=ACCENT_BLUE)

# Title
draw_centered_text(y, "JS Framework Benchmark", title_font, TEXT_PRIMARY)
y += 170

# Subtitle
draw_centered_text(y, "5 Years of Browser Performance Testing", subtitle_font, TEXT_SECONDARY)
y += 100

# One-liner
one_liner = "Tracking JavaScript framework performance across Chrome 55 → 146"
draw_centered_text(y, one_liner, small_font, TEXT_MUTED)
y += 100

# ============================================================
# HERO METRICS ROW
# ============================================================
hero_y = y
hero_h = 340
draw_rounded_rect(MARGIN, hero_y, CONTENT_W, hero_h, 24, BG_CARD, outline=BORDER)

heroes = [
    ("60+", "Official Runs", ACCENT_BLUE),
    ("55 → 146", "Chrome Versions", ACCENT_TEAL),
    ("~8 Years", "Of Benchmarking", ACCENT_AMBER),
]
hero_cell_w = CONTENT_W // 3
for i, (value, label, color) in enumerate(heroes):
    cx = MARGIN + hero_cell_w * i + hero_cell_w // 2
    vw = text_width(value, hero_font)
    draw.text((cx - vw // 2, hero_y + 40), value, font=hero_font, fill=color)
    lw = text_width(label, hero_label_font)
    draw.text((cx - lw // 2, hero_y + 255), label, font=hero_label_font, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
    if i < 2:
        div_x = MARGIN + hero_cell_w * (i + 1)
        draw.line([(div_x, hero_y + 50), (div_x, hero_y + hero_h - 50)], fill=BORDER, width=2)

y = hero_y + hero_h + 80

# ============================================================
# SECTION 1: OVERVIEW
# ============================================================
draw_hline(y)
y += 50

draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y, MARGIN + 8, y + 64], fill=ACCENT_BLUE)
draw.text((MARGIN + 30, y - 4), "What Is the JS Framework Benchmark?", font=section_font, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
y += 100

overview_lines = [
    "The most widely referenced open-source benchmark for comparing JavaScript",
    "web frameworks on real-world DOM operations. Maintained by Stefan Krause,",
    "it measures creating 1,000 rows, partial updates, row selection, swapping,",
    "removal, and startup time — all inside a real Chrome browser with controlled",
    "CPU throttling.",
]
for line in overview_lines:
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), line, font=body_font, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
    y += 60

y += 70

# ============================================================
# SECTION 2: TIMELINE (CENTERPIECE)
# ============================================================
draw_hline(y)
y += 50

draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y, MARGIN + 8, y + 64], fill=ACCENT_TEAL)
draw.text((MARGIN + 30, y - 4), "Benchmark Timeline: Chrome 55 → Chrome 146", font=section_font, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
y += 110

timeline_data = [
    {"year": "2017–19", "chrome": "55, 58, 62, 69", "runs": 4, "notes": "Early era; hosted on stefankrause.net", "highlight": False},
    {"year": "2020", "chrome": "83 – 87", "runs": 5, "notes": "Migrated to GitHub Pages", "highlight": False},
    {"year": "2021", "chrome": "88 – 96", "runs": 9, "notes": "Steady monthly cadence established", "highlight": False},
    {"year": "2022", "chrome": "97 – 108", "runs": 13, "notes": "Includes 2 Windows runs (Chrome 104)", "highlight": False},
    {"year": "2023", "chrome": "109 – 120", "runs": 12, "notes": "Major methodology overhaul at Chrome 118", "highlight": True},
    {"year": "2024", "chrome": "121 – 131", "runs": 12, "notes": "Includes 1 Windows run (Chrome 121)", "highlight": False},
    {"year": "2025", "chrome": "132 – 143", "runs": 12, "notes": "Most active year; alternating keyed-only", "highlight": False},
    {"year": "2026", "chrome": "144 – 146", "runs": 3, "notes": "Latest: Chrome 146 on macOS", "highlight": False},
]

row_h = 115
bar_max_w = 500
max_runs = 13

col_year_x = MARGIN + 20
col_chrome_x = MARGIN + 320
col_bar_x = MARGIN + 680
col_runs_x = col_bar_x + bar_max_w + 40
col_notes_x = col_runs_x + 120

# Header
draw.text((col_year_x, y), "YEAR", font=small_bold_font, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
draw.text((col_chrome_x, y), "CHROME", font=small_bold_font, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
draw.text((col_bar_x, y), "RUNS", font=small_bold_font, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
draw.text((col_notes_x, y), "NOTES", font=small_bold_font, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
y += 65

for entry in timeline_data:
    row_bg = HIGHLIGHT_BG if entry["highlight"] else None
    if row_bg:
        draw_rounded_rect(MARGIN, y - 12, CONTENT_W, row_h, 12, row_bg, outline=ACCENT_AMBER, outline_width=3)

    year_color = ACCENT_AMBER if entry["highlight"] else ACCENT_BLUE
    draw.text((col_year_x, y + 20), entry["year"], font=timeline_year_font, fill=year_color)
    draw.text((col_chrome_x, y + 26), entry["chrome"], font=timeline_chrome_font, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)

    bar_w = int((entry["runs"] / max_runs) * bar_max_w)
    bar_color = ACCENT_AMBER if entry["highlight"] else ACCENT_TEAL
    draw_rounded_rect(col_bar_x, y + 30, bar_w, 40, 8, bar_color)

    draw.text((col_runs_x, y + 24), str(entry["runs"]), font=mono_bold_font, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)

    note_color = ACCENT_AMBER if entry["highlight"] else TEXT_MUTED
    draw.text((col_notes_x, y + 30), entry["notes"], font=timeline_note_font, fill=note_color)

    y += row_h

y += 50

# ============================================================
# CAUTION CALLOUT — Chrome 118
# ============================================================
caution_h = 220
draw_rounded_rect(MARGIN, y, CONTENT_W, caution_h, 18, "#2D1F00", outline=ACCENT_AMBER, outline_width=4)

# Warning triangle
tri_cx = MARGIN + 50
tri_cy = y + caution_h // 2
tri_s = 40
draw.polygon([
    (tri_cx, tri_cy - tri_s),
    (tri_cx - tri_s, tri_cy + tri_s),
    (tri_cx + tri_s, tri_cy + tri_s),
], fill=ACCENT_AMBER)
draw.text((tri_cx - 10, tri_cy - 20), "!", font=load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 44), fill="#2D1F00")

draw.text((MARGIN + 120, y + 35), "METHODOLOGY BREAK AT CHROME 118", font=warning_font, fill=ACCENT_AMBER)
caution_lines = [
    "Scoring switched from arithmetic mean to weighted geometric mean. CPU throttling was",
    "recalibrated. Cross-version comparisons before and after Chrome 118 are unreliable.",
]
cy = y + 100
for line in caution_lines:
    draw.text((MARGIN + 120, cy), line, font=caution_font, fill="#F0D68A")
    cy += 52

y += caution_h + 80

# ============================================================
# SECTION 3: METHODOLOGY MILESTONES
# ============================================================
draw_hline(y)
y += 50

draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y, MARGIN + 8, y + 64], fill=ACCENT_AMBER)
draw.text((MARGIN + 30, y - 4), "Methodology Milestones", font=section_font, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
y += 110

milestones = [
    ("Chrome 118", "2023", "Weighted Geometric Mean", "Score switched from arithmetic to weighted geometric mean", ACCENT_AMBER),
    ("Chrome 118", "2023", "CPU Throttling Adjustment", "Throttling factors recalibrated for realistic load simulation", ACCENT_AMBER),
    ("Chrome 118+", "2023–now", "Measurement Fine-Tuning", "Ongoing refinements to timing and driver instrumentation", ACCENT_TEAL),
    ("Chrome 139+", "2025–26", "Keyed-Only Alternation", "Odd Chrome versions benchmark keyed frameworks only", ACCENT_BLUE),
]

card_h = 155
card_gap = 24
cards_per_row = 2
card_w = (CONTENT_W - card_gap) // cards_per_row

for i, (chrome, year, title, desc, color) in enumerate(milestones):
    col = i % cards_per_row
    row = i // cards_per_row
    cx = MARGIN + col * (card_w + card_gap)
    cy_card = y + row * (card_h + card_gap)

    draw_rounded_rect(cx, cy_card, card_w, card_h, 14, BG_CARD, outline=BORDER)
    draw.rectangle([cx, cy_card, cx + 6, cy_card + card_h], fill=color)

    badge_text = chrome
    bw = text_width(badge_text, mono_small) + 24
    draw_rounded_rect(cx + 30, cy_card + 20, bw, 42, 8, color + "22")
    draw.text((cx + 42, cy_card + 22), badge_text, font=mono_small, fill=color)

    draw.text((cx + 56 + bw, cy_card + 24), year, font=small_font, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
    draw.text((cx + 30, cy_card + 72), title, font=body_bold_font, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
    draw.text((cx + 30, cy_card + 120), desc, font=small_font, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)

y += (card_h + card_gap) * 2 + 70

# ============================================================
# SECTION 4: PLATFORM & COVERAGE
# ============================================================
draw_hline(y)
y += 50

draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y, MARGIN + 8, y + 64], fill=ACCENT_BLUE)
draw.text((MARGIN + 30, y - 4), "Platform & Framework Coverage", font=section_font, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
y += 110

left_w = CONTENT_W // 2 - 20
right_w = CONTENT_W // 2 - 20

# Left: platform card
plat_h = 380
draw_rounded_rect(MARGIN, y, left_w, plat_h, 18, BG_CARD, outline=BORDER)

draw.text((MARGIN + 40, y + 30), "PRIMARY PLATFORM", font=small_bold_font, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
draw.text((MARGIN + 40, y + 85), "macOS (OSX)", font=metric_value_font, fill=ACCENT_TEAL)
draw.text((MARGIN + 40, y + 185), "95%+ of all runs on macOS + Chrome", font=small_font, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)

bar_total_w = left_w - 80
macos_bar_w = int(bar_total_w * 0.97)
win_bar_w = max(bar_total_w - macos_bar_w, 12)
bar_y2 = y + 250

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate the JS Framework Benchmark poster as a single PNG image."""

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
import os

# --- Dimensions: A1 portrait at 150 DPI ---
W, H = 3508, 4961

# --- Color palette: dark-mode developer aesthetic ---
BG = "#0D1117"
BG_CARD = "#161B22"
BG_CARD_ALT = "#1C2333"
ACCENT_BLUE = "#58A6FF"
ACCENT_TEAL = "#3FB9A0"
ACCENT_AMBER = "#F0B429"
TEXT_PRIMARY = "#E6EDF3"
TEXT_SECONDARY = "#8B949E"
TEXT_MUTED = "#6E7681"
GRID_LINE = "#21262D"
BORDER = "#30363D"
HIGHLIGHT_BG = "#1A1F2E"

# --- Fonts ---
def load_font(path, size):
    try:
        return ImageFont.truetype(path, size)
    except:
        return ImageFont.load_default()

FONT_MONO = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSansMono.ttf"
FONT_MONO_BOLD = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSansMono-Bold.ttf"
FONT_SANS = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/liberation/LiberationSans-Regular.ttf"
FONT_SANS_BOLD = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/liberation/LiberationSans-Bold.ttf"

title_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 130)
subtitle_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 58)
section_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 68)
body_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 44)
body_bold_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 44)
small_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 38)
small_bold_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 38)
mono_small = load_font(FONT_MONO, 36)
mono_bold_font = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 44)
hero_font = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 190)
hero_label_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 48)
metric_value_font = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 76)
timeline_year_font = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 50)
timeline_chrome_font = load_font(FONT_MONO, 36)
timeline_note_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 34)
takeaway_num_font = load_font(FONT_MONO_BOLD, 58)
warning_font = load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 48)
caution_font = load_font(FONT_SANS, 40)

img = Image.new("RGB", (W, H), BG)
draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img)

MARGIN = 140
CONTENT_W = W - 2 * MARGIN

# --- Helper functions ---
def draw_rounded_rect(x, y, w, h, radius, fill, outline=None, outline_width=2):
    draw.rounded_rectangle([x, y, x + w, y + h], radius=radius, fill=fill, outline=outline, width=outline_width)

def draw_dot_grid(x, y, w, h, spacing=40, color="#161B22"):
    for gx in range(x, x + w, spacing):
        for gy in range(y, y + h, spacing):
            draw.ellipse([gx - 1, gy - 1, gx + 1, gy + 1], fill=color)

def text_width(text, font):
    bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), text, font=font)
    return bbox[2] - bbox[0]

def draw_centered_text(y, text, font, fill):
    tw = text_width(text, font)
    draw.text(((W - tw) // 2, y), text, font=font, fill=fill)

def draw_hline(y, color=GRID_LINE, width=2):
    draw.line([(MARGIN, y), (W - MARGIN, y)], fill=color, width=width)

# --- Subtle background dot grid ---
draw_dot_grid(0, 0, W, H, spacing=48, color="#161B22")

# ============================================================
# HEADER SECTION
# ============================================================
y = 100

# Accent line top
draw.rectangle([0, 0, W, 8], fill=ACCENT_BLUE)

# Title
draw_centered_text(y, "JS Framework Benchmark", title_font, TEXT_PRIMARY)
y += 170

# Subtitle
draw_centered_text(y, "5 Years of Browser Performance Testing", subtitle_font, TEXT_SECONDARY)
y += 100

# One-liner
one_liner = "Tracking JavaScript framework performance across Chrome 55 → 146"
draw_centered_text(y, one_liner, small_font, TEXT_MUTED)
y += 100

# ============================================================
# HERO METRICS ROW
# ============================================================
hero_y = y
hero_h = 340
draw_rounded_rect(MARGIN, hero_y, CONTENT_W, hero_h, 24, BG_CARD, outline=BORDER)

heroes = [
    ("60+", "Official Runs", ACCENT_BLUE),
    ("55 → 146", "Chrome Versions", ACCENT_TEAL),
    ("~8 Years", "Of Benchmarking", ACCENT_AMBER),
]
hero_cell_w = CONTENT_W // 3
for i, (value, label, color) in enumerate(heroes):
    cx = MARGIN + hero_cell_w * i + hero_cell_w // 2
    vw = text_width(value, hero_font)
    draw.text((cx - vw // 2, hero_y + 40), value, font=hero_font, fill=color)
    lw = text_width(label, hero_label_font)
    draw.text((cx - lw // 2, hero_y + 255), label, font=hero_label_font, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
    if i < 2:
        div_x = MARGIN + hero_cell_w * (i + 1)
        draw.line([(div_x, hero_y + 50), (div_x, hero_y + hero_h - 50)], fill=BORDER, width=2)

y = hero_y + hero_h + 80

# ============================================================
# SECTION 1: OVERVIEW
# ============================================================
draw_hline(y)
y += 50

draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y, MARGIN + 8, y + 64], fill=ACCENT_BLUE)
draw.text((MARGIN + 30, y - 4), "What Is the JS Framework Benchmark?", font=section_font, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
y += 100

overview_lines = [
    "The most widely referenced open-source benchmark for comparing JavaScript",
    "web frameworks on real-world DOM operations. Maintained by Stefan Krause,",
    "it measures creating 1,000 rows, partial updates, row selection, swapping,",
    "removal, and startup time — all inside a real Chrome browser with controlled",
    "CPU throttling.",
]
for line in overview_lines:
    draw.text((MARGIN, y), line, font=body_font, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)
    y += 60

y += 70

# ============================================================
# SECTION 2: TIMELINE (CENTERPIECE)
# ============================================================
draw_hline(y)
y += 50

draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y, MARGIN + 8, y + 64], fill=ACCENT_TEAL)
draw.text((MARGIN + 30, y - 4), "Benchmark Timeline: Chrome 55 → Chrome 146", font=section_font, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
y += 110

timeline_data = [
    {"year": "2017–19", "chrome": "55, 58, 62, 69", "runs": 4, "notes": "Early era; hosted on stefankrause.net", "highlight": False},
    {"year": "2020", "chrome": "83 – 87", "runs": 5, "notes": "Migrated to GitHub Pages", "highlight": False},
    {"year": "2021", "chrome": "88 – 96", "runs": 9, "notes": "Steady monthly cadence established", "highlight": False},
    {"year": "2022", "chrome": "97 – 108", "runs": 13, "notes": "Includes 2 Windows runs (Chrome 104)", "highlight": False},
    {"year": "2023", "chrome": "109 – 120", "runs": 12, "notes": "Major methodology overhaul at Chrome 118", "highlight": True},
    {"year": "2024", "chrome": "121 – 131", "runs": 12, "notes": "Includes 1 Windows run (Chrome 121)", "highlight": False},
    {"year": "2025", "chrome": "132 – 143", "runs": 12, "notes": "Most active year; alternating keyed-only", "highlight": False},
    {"year": "2026", "chrome": "144 – 146", "runs": 3, "notes": "Latest: Chrome 146 on macOS", "highlight": False},
]

row_h = 115
bar_max_w = 500
max_runs = 13

col_year_x = MARGIN + 20
col_chrome_x = MARGIN + 320
col_bar_x = MARGIN + 680
col_runs_x = col_bar_x + bar_max_w + 40
col_notes_x = col_runs_x + 120

# Header
draw.text((col_year_x, y), "YEAR", font=small_bold_font, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
draw.text((col_chrome_x, y), "CHROME", font=small_bold_font, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
draw.text((col_bar_x, y), "RUNS", font=small_bold_font, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
draw.text((col_notes_x, y), "NOTES", font=small_bold_font, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
y += 65

for entry in timeline_data:
    row_bg = HIGHLIGHT_BG if entry["highlight"] else None
    if row_bg:
        draw_rounded_rect(MARGIN, y - 12, CONTENT_W, row_h, 12, row_bg, outline=ACCENT_AMBER, outline_width=3)

    year_color = ACCENT_AMBER if entry["highlight"] else ACCENT_BLUE
    draw.text((col_year_x, y + 20), entry["year"], font=timeline_year_font, fill=year_color)
    draw.text((col_chrome_x, y + 26), entry["chrome"], font=timeline_chrome_font, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)

    bar_w = int((entry["runs"] / max_runs) * bar_max_w)
    bar_color = ACCENT_AMBER if entry["highlight"] else ACCENT_TEAL
    draw_rounded_rect(col_bar_x, y + 30, bar_w, 40, 8, bar_color)

    draw.text((col_runs_x, y + 24), str(entry["runs"]), font=mono_bold_font, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)

    note_color = ACCENT_AMBER if entry["highlight"] else TEXT_MUTED
    draw.text((col_notes_x, y + 30), entry["notes"], font=timeline_note_font, fill=note_color)

    y += row_h

y += 50

# ============================================================
# CAUTION CALLOUT — Chrome 118
# ============================================================
caution_h = 220
draw_rounded_rect(MARGIN, y, CONTENT_W, caution_h, 18, "#2D1F00", outline=ACCENT_AMBER, outline_width=4)

# Warning triangle
tri_cx = MARGIN + 50
tri_cy = y + caution_h // 2
tri_s = 40
draw.polygon([
    (tri_cx, tri_cy - tri_s),
    (tri_cx - tri_s, tri_cy + tri_s),
    (tri_cx + tri_s, tri_cy + tri_s),
], fill=ACCENT_AMBER)
draw.text((tri_cx - 10, tri_cy - 20), "!", font=load_font(FONT_SANS_BOLD, 44), fill="#2D1F00")

draw.text((MARGIN + 120, y + 35), "METHODOLOGY BREAK AT CHROME 118", font=warning_font, fill=ACCENT_AMBER)
caution_lines = [
    "Scoring switched from arithmetic mean to weighted geometric mean. CPU throttling was",
    "recalibrated. Cross-version comparisons before and after Chrome 118 are unreliable.",
]
cy = y + 100
for line in caution_lines:
    draw.text((MARGIN + 120, cy), line, font=caution_font, fill="#F0D68A")
    cy += 52

y += caution_h + 80

# ============================================================
# SECTION 3: METHODOLOGY MILESTONES
# ============================================================
draw_hline(y)
y += 50

draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y, MARGIN + 8, y + 64], fill=ACCENT_AMBER)
draw.text((MARGIN + 30, y - 4), "Methodology Milestones", font=section_font, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
y += 110

milestones = [
    ("Chrome 118", "2023", "Weighted Geometric Mean", "Score switched from arithmetic to weighted geometric mean", ACCENT_AMBER),
    ("Chrome 118", "2023", "CPU Throttling Adjustment", "Throttling factors recalibrated for realistic load simulation", ACCENT_AMBER),
    ("Chrome 118+", "2023–now", "Measurement Fine-Tuning", "Ongoing refinements to timing and driver instrumentation", ACCENT_TEAL),
    ("Chrome 139+", "2025–26", "Keyed-Only Alternation", "Odd Chrome versions benchmark keyed frameworks only", ACCENT_BLUE),
]

card_h = 155
card_gap = 24
cards_per_row = 2
card_w = (CONTENT_W - card_gap) // cards_per_row

for i, (chrome, year, title, desc, color) in enumerate(milestones):
    col = i % cards_per_row
    row = i // cards_per_row
    cx = MARGIN + col * (card_w + card_gap)
    cy_card = y + row * (card_h + card_gap)

    draw_rounded_rect(cx, cy_card, card_w, card_h, 14, BG_CARD, outline=BORDER)
    draw.rectangle([cx, cy_card, cx + 6, cy_card + card_h], fill=color)

    badge_text = chrome
    bw = text_width(badge_text, mono_small) + 24
    draw_rounded_rect(cx + 30, cy_card + 20, bw, 42, 8, color + "22")
    draw.text((cx + 42, cy_card + 22), badge_text, font=mono_small, fill=color)

    draw.text((cx + 56 + bw, cy_card + 24), year, font=small_font, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
    draw.text((cx + 30, cy_card + 72), title, font=body_bold_font, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
    draw.text((cx + 30, cy_card + 120), desc, font=small_font, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)

y += (card_h + card_gap) * 2 + 70

# ============================================================
# SECTION 4: PLATFORM & COVERAGE
# ============================================================
draw_hline(y)
y += 50

draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y, MARGIN + 8, y + 64], fill=ACCENT_BLUE)
draw.text((MARGIN + 30, y - 4), "Platform & Framework Coverage", font=section_font, fill=TEXT_PRIMARY)
y += 110

left_w = CONTENT_W // 2 - 20
right_w = CONTENT_W // 2 - 20

# Left: platform card
plat_h = 380
draw_rounded_rect(MARGIN, y, left_w, plat_h, 18, BG_CARD, outline=BORDER)

draw.text((MARGIN + 40, y + 30), "PRIMARY PLATFORM", font=small_bold_font, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
draw.text((MARGIN + 40, y + 85), "macOS (OSX)", font=metric_value_font, fill=ACCENT_TEAL)
draw.text((MARGIN + 40, y + 185), "95%+ of all runs on macOS + Chrome", font=small_font, fill=TEXT_SECONDARY)

bar_total_w = left_w - 80
macos_bar_w = int(bar_total_w * 0.97)
win_bar_w = max(bar_total_w - macos_bar_w, 12)
bar_y2 = y + 250
draw_rounded_rect(MARGIN + 40, bar_y2, macos_bar_w, 40, 8, ACCENT_TEAL)
draw_rounded_rect(MARGIN + 40 + macos_bar_w + 6, bar_y2, win_bar_w, 40, 8, ACCENT_BLUE)
draw.text((MARGIN + 40, bar_y2 + 55), "macOS: 58+ runs", font=small_font, fill=ACCENT_TEAL)
draw.text((MARGIN + 40 + left_w // 2, bar_y2 + 55), "Windows: 2 runs", font=small_font, fill=ACCENT_BLUE)

# Right: metrics grid
right_x = MARGIN + left_w + 40
draw_rounded_rect(right_x, y, right_w, plat_h, 18, BG_CARD, outline=BORDER)

metrics = [
    ("12", "Runs in 2025", "Most active year", ACCENT_BLUE),
    ("Chr 146", "Latest Run", "macOS, mid-2026", ACCENT_TEAL),
    ("2", "Windows Runs", "Chrome 104 & 121", ACCENT_AMBER),
    ("Keyed/Non", "Framework Modes", "Alternating since v139", ACCENT_BLUE),
]

met_cols = 2
